description: Replace the single hardcoded PS1 core declaration in native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift with a table of five core declarations, make ensureCoreLoaded take a coreId, widen the importable and launchable extension sets to every system the app now ships, and route a tapped game to its core through ONE extension-to-core mapping that both the Library row and the launch path consult. No Rust change is needed: NativeLibretroCore is core-agnostic and CoreRegistry already holds many declared cores. Swift only.
steps: Add a top-level CoreSpec value type (coreId, displayName, systems, the dylib filename, base and max geometry, aspect ratio, fps, sample rate, pixel format, priority, optional BIOS filenames) and a top-level CoreCatalog holding the five specs. Top-level rather than nested privately inside EngineHost, because the Library row needs the same routing table and a second copy of it is the bug this feature exists to prevent.

Populate the table with exactly the declared values: fceumm, systems [nes], base 256x240, 60.0988 fps, 48000 Hz, pixelFormat 0, priority 100. snes9x, systems [snes], base 256x224, 60.0988 fps, 32040 Hz, pixelFormat 0, priority 100. mgba, systems [gba, gb, gbc], base 240x160, 59.7275 fps, 65536 Hz, pixelFormat 0, priority 100. genesis_plus_gx, systems [genesis, sms, gg], base 320x224 with a max of 348x240 so a 256x192 Master System frame and a 320x240 Mega Drive frame both fit, 59.9227 fps, 44100 Hz, pixelFormat 0, priority 100. pcsx_rearmed keeps its existing values unchanged (320x240 base, 700x576 max, 59.94 fps, 44100 Hz, pixelFormat 0, priority 0, its six BIOS filenames). Maxima and aspect ratios come from web/cores/manifest.json, which already declares these same four cores for the web build.

Comment, once and clearly, that pixelFormat 0 is the BRIDGE's numbering (0 = RGB565 per CoreDeclaration) and not libretro's, and that geometry, fps and sample rate are pre-load hints only: sync_descriptor_from_core overwrites them from retro_get_system_av_info the moment the core loads and the pixel format is renegotiated through SET_PIXEL_FORMAT inside retro_load_game. Note specifically that fceumm's iOS makefile forces WANT_32BPP, so that core will negotiate XRGB8888 on device even though it is declared as RGB565, and that this is correct rather than a bug to fix.

Add CoreCatalog.routes, the single lowercased-extension to coreId mapping: nes -> fceumm; sfc, smc -> snes9x; gba, gb, gbc -> mgba; sms, gg, md, gen -> genesis_plus_gx; cue, chd, pbp, iso -> pcsx_rearmed. Add core(forExtension:) and core(id:) lookups. An extension with no mapped core must return nil so the caller can write its own distinct HUD line rather than failing silently.

Move the extension sets into CoreCatalog: importableExtensions = nes, sfc, smc, gba, gb, gbc, sms, md, gen, gg, cue, bin, chd, pbp, iso, and launchableExtensions DERIVED as importableExtensions minus bin, so the two can never drift apart. Comment that a .bin is a CD track a cue sheet names literally and is therefore importable but never a launch target.

Change ensureCoreLoaded() to ensureCoreLoaded(coreId:). PRESERVE THE FIX FROM THE PREVIOUS TURN: read engine.coreState(coreId:) fresh on every call as the single source of truth, keep no cached Bool anywhere, treat only loaded and bound as usable, collapse a nil state to unknown, and after declare plus load RE-READ the state instead of inferring success from nothing having thrown. Keep the per-core dylib existence pre-check and every distinct HUD string, generalised to name the core.

Add declareAllCores(), called once when the surface attaches, that declares all five cores and reports how many were declared plus any whose dylib is missing from the bundle. Comment that declaring loads no code (declare_core only stores metadata and touches no filesystem) so declaring five is cheap, and that only the core a tapped game needs is ever loaded, which is what preserves the project's dynamic-loading rule.
Add a published `cores` HUD line for that declaration summary, rendered like the existing bios line only when non-empty, so a dylib that failed to embed is visible before the user taps anything.

Rewrite launch(entry:) to route by extension: keep the unconditional opening breadcrumb first, resolve the core through CoreCatalog and write a distinct HUD line if the extension maps to nothing, then stop any running session, then call ensureCoreLoaded(coreId:). KEEP THE ALL-CAPS ORDERING COMMENT: the stop must come first because stopSession -> engine.stop() unloads the core under the Drop retention policy, so a check before the stop would verify a core the stop then invalidates. Name the coreId in the opening, the state breadcrumb, the running line and the failure line, so a wrong-core routing bug is visible immediately.

Generalise the surrounding PS1-only wording: the file header, the import rejection line (which now lists the supported extensions rather than saying 'not PS1 content'), the nothing-launchable library line, the empty-state guidance, the attach-ready line and the HUD title.
Make the Library row show which core will run the entry, taken from the same routes table, so a routing mistake is legible in the list before anything is launched.

Keep every architectural invariant: import-and-copy into Documents with original filenames and no rename-on-collision, collision replaces via removeItem then copyItem, per-file do/catch; no security-scoped URLs on the launch path and no activeScopedURL or failAfterScope; the picker stays [UTType.item] with asCopy: true and allowsMultipleSelection, the strongly retained delegate, activePicker retention, all four @objc callbacks with outcomeDelivered suppression, present(_:animated:completion:) with the picker-is-up line inside the completion, topmostViewController(), and the Task { @MainActor in } hops that bind `let host = self.host` first; one MTLDevice owned by Rust; no changes to MetalCanvas or the graphics path.
Sweep for em dashes and make sure every new failure path writes a distinct HUD string.
acceptance_criteria: Five cores are declared with exactly the specified ids, systems, geometry, fps, sample rates, pixel formats and priorities, and each spec carries the dylib filename that matches FEAT-001's canonical name byte for byte.
ensureCoreLoaded(coreId:) takes the core id, reads engine.coreState(coreId:) on every call, keeps no cached Bool, and re-reads the state after declare plus load instead of assuming success.
importableExtensions is nes, sfc, smc, gba, gb, gbc, sms, md, gen, gg, cue, bin, chd, pbp, iso and launchableExtensions is that set minus bin, derived rather than restated.
Exactly one extension-to-core mapping exists in the file, and both the Library row and launch(entry:) read it.
An extension with no mapped core produces a distinct HUD line and no launch attempt.
ensureCoreLoaded(coreId:) is still called after stopSession() in launch(entry:), and the all-caps ordering comment is still there.
The HUD names the core in the opening line, the running line and the failure lines.
The import-and-copy behaviour, the absence of security scopes on the launch path, the picker configuration and its delegate lifetime machinery, and the Metal path are all unchanged.
swiftc -frontend -parse exits 0 and no em dashes remain in the file.
verification: swiftc -frontend -parse native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift and native/ios/MetalCanvas.swift -> exit 0, plus a by-eye review because this sandbox cannot type-check SwiftUI, UIKit or the generated UniFFI facade: the core table's UInt32/Double/Float/Int32 literals, the coreState Optional handling, List/ForEach identity and the extension routing.

grep to confirm: no cached load flag; ensureCoreLoaded takes coreId; five dylib filenames present; exactly one engine.launch call site; SecurityScopedResource only as the single defensive pair inside importFiles; no activeScopedURL or failAfterScope; UTType.item still the only picker type; all four @objc callbacks present.
cargo test and cargo test --features native-core,uniffi-bindings -> 74 and 84 passing, proving no Rust was touched.
On-device import and launch of a .nes, .sfc, .gba, .sms, .md and a PS1 cue/bin is verified only by the orchestrator's device run.
findings: native/ios/ContinuumApp.swift went from 1203 to 1327 lines. Added top-level `struct CoreSpec: Sendable` and `enum CoreCatalog` holding fceumm, snes9x, mgba, genesisPlusGx and pcsxReARMed with exactly the specified values (fceumm 256x240 / 60.0988 / 48000, snes9x 256x224 / 60.0988 / 32040, mgba 240x160 / 59.7275 / 65536, genesis_plus_gx 320x224 base with a 348x240 max that covers both a 256x192 Master System frame and a 320x240 Mega Drive frame / 59.9227 / 44100, all pixelFormat 0 and priority 100; pcsx_rearmed unchanged at 320x240 / 700x576 / 59.94 / 44100 / priority 0 with its six BIOS filenames). Maxima and aspect ratios match web/cores/manifest.json for the four cores the web build also ships. CoreCatalog also owns the ONE routing table (routes, built from the specs' own coreIds so an id cannot be misspelled on one side), importableExtensions (15 entries) and launchableExtensions DERIVED as importable minus the track extension, plus core(id:), core(forExtension:), routeLabel and extensionList. EngineHost lost `private enum PS1` and its two extension arrays and gained @Published cores, declaration(for:modulePath:), declareAllCores(), biosStatus(for:in:) and ensureCoreLoaded(coreId:). launch(entry:) resolves the core BEFORE the re-entrancy stop so an unmapped extension cannot tear down a running game just to report itself, keeps the all-caps ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING comment and the after-stopSession call site, and names the coreId in the opening, state, running and failure lines. The Library row's detail line ends with the routed coreId, so a wrong route is visible before a tap. Two review findings were fixed: the BIOS HUD line used to be written at attach as a side effect of loading PCSX ReARMed, and since nothing loads at attach any more it is now written by declareAllCores (knowing a BIOS is absent is only useful before a disc is tapped), and biosStatus now names the core in all three branches rather than one, because the line appears and disappears as different cores load. VERIFIED: swiftc -frontend -parse exits 0 on both Swift files (parse only, so the core table's types, the coreState Optional handling, List/ForEach identity and the routing were reviewed by eye and by a semantic review pass); no PS1. references remain; exactly one engine.launch call site; SecurityScopedResource appears only as the single defensive pair inside importFiles; no cached load flag anywhere; four @objc callbacks; [UTType.item] + asCopy + allowsMultipleSelection intact; no em dashes; a scripted check proves the launchable set (14) equals the routes key set and that .bin is importable but has no route; cargo test 74 and 84 passing, so no Rust was touched.
